reference.source: Volpe's Neurology of the Newborn / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A malformation of neuronal migration in which nodules of grey matter fail to migrate and remain lining the walls of the lateral ventricles
On MRI the nodules follow grey-matter signal on all sequences, are typically smooth and rounded, and do not enhance, distinguishing them from subependymal tumours
The classic form is X-linked, caused by FLNA (filamin A) variants, and is often bilateral and nodular; it is usually lethal in males, so most affected individuals are female

FLNA-related heterotopia carries systemic associations including cardiovascular anomalies such as aortic and valvular disease, and a bleeding or connective-tissue tendency, warranting cardiac surveillance
The autosomal recessive form due to ARFGEF2 is associated with microcephaly and more severe developmental impairment
Many individuals present in adolescence or adulthood with focal epilepsy and otherwise normal or near-normal intellect, particularly in the FLNA form
Diagnosis is by MRI recognition of grey-matter nodules along the ventricular margin combined with targeted genetic testing
reference.pathophysiology: Periventricular nodular heterotopia results from failure of neurons to migrate away from the germinal (ventricular) zone during cortical development, so that collections of neurons persist as nodules along the ependymal lining of the lateral ventricles. The X-linked form is caused by variants in FLNA, which encodes filamin A, an actin-binding protein required for the cytoskeletal dynamics that drive early neuronal migration and also important in vascular and connective tissue, explaining the cardiovascular associations. The autosomal recessive ARFGEF2 form disrupts vesicle trafficking needed for migration and proliferation, producing microcephaly with heterotopia.
additionalDifferentials: Subependymal nodules of tuberous sclerosis, which may calcify and enhance
Subependymal spread of tumour or subependymoma
Subcortical band heterotopia and other heterotopia patterns
Grey-matter signal artefact along the ventricle
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI to identify grey-matter-signal nodules lining the ventricles and any cortical involvement
Molecular genetic testing including FLNA analysis and, where indicated, ARFGEF2
Cardiac evaluation with echocardiography and aortic imaging in FLNA-related disease
Assessment for bleeding tendency and connective-tissue features in FLNA variants
redFlags: Aortic dilatation, valvular disease, or other cardiovascular complications in FLNA-related heterotopia
Bleeding tendency associated with filamin A dysfunction
Microcephaly with severe developmental impairment suggesting the ARFGEF2 form
reference.prognosis: In the common FLNA-related form, many individuals have normal or near-normal cognition with focal epilepsy that is often manageable, though cardiovascular and vascular complications can affect long-term health. The ARFGEF2 form and syndromic presentations carry a poorer neurodevelopmental prognosis.
pitfalls: Mistaking heterotopic nodules for the enhancing, sometimes calcified subependymal nodules of tuberous sclerosis
Failing to arrange cardiovascular surveillance in FLNA-related disease
Overlooking X-linked inheritance and its implications for male fetal loss and family counselling
Attributing new focal seizures in an adult to another cause without considering heterotopia on MRI
